title: An AI-Driven Kidney-Friendly Recipe Recommendation and Meal-Planning Tool for Personalized Nutrition
content: Background/Objectives: Patients with chronic kidney disease need more than dietary advice: they need meal options that fit their nutritional requirements, food preferences, and daily routines. We developed and evaluated an artificial intelligence (AI) application for personalized recipe selection and meal planning. Methods: Retrieval-augmented generation connects AI with 1,041 curated kidney-friendly recipes. Testing covered recipe recommendations (36 requests) and screening for inappropriate inputs (100 requests), each repeated 30 times. A researcher with nutrition training assessed AI-generated meal plans for seven clinical scenarios. Results: The application supports searching and saving recipes, meal planning around dietitian-informed nutrient targets, daily nutrient summaries, and exports with source links. The average percentage of recommended recipes meeting the requested criteria was 93.67% for dietary restrictions and 90.57% for nutrient requirements. Input screening correctly accepted or rejected 96.77% of requests. All meal plans with nutrient targets entered through dedicated fields met those targets according to application-reported totals. However, review identified concerns about portion sizes and meal completeness, and nutrient totals were not independently verified. Conclusions: This integrated application offers a foundation for dietitian-guided nutrition support grounded in documented recipes. Further refinement and evaluation with patients and dietitians are needed to address complex requests, nutritional completeness, and practical value.
